 Order

Applicant is in detention since 09.10.2024.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 08.10.2024, 20 years old prosecutrix lodged an FIR stating that in her grocery shop applicant committed sexual intercourse with her.
Now, she is carrying pregnancy.
It was further alleged that on 03.10.2023, she had gone with Badal Saket to Puna.
Badal had asked her to abort the child, but when she refused to do so, he abused and refused to keep her with him.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12200 2 MCRC-2375-2025 3.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
They were having love affairs and were having consensual sexual relationship and on account of those relationship prosecutrix became pregnant.
Charge sheet has been filed.
As parties are major, no offence of rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault is made out.

Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail pending the Badal Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199605784/
1 trial.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant but counsel for the objector/victim has submitted that applicant be released on bail as both were having consensual sexual relations with each other and applicant is ready to enter into wedlock with the prosecutrix.
5.
Charge sheet has already been filed.

Having taken into consideration the prosecutrix's statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS and other material available on record, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I deem it a fit case for grant of bail.

Consequently, this bail application under 483 of BNSS, 2023/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant,
stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant - Badal Saket be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12200 3 MCRC-2375-2025 under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023/437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Badal Saket vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199605784/
